subject: Martin Luther King Jr. Day Celebration
overview: The West Medford Community Center hosted its second annual celebration to honor Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., featuring dramatic performances, music, and the presentation of community leadership awards. The event focused on the concept of the 'beloved community' and featured a keynote address on law enforcement reform and nonviolence.

items.title: Invocation and Opening
items.summary: Stacey Moore offered an invocation calling for the community to be champions of equity, equality, and justice.

items.title: Official Welcomes
items.summary: Executive Director Lisa M. Crossman and Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn welcomed attendees and spoke on the city's efforts to solidify trust and serve historically marginalized residents.

items.title: Musical and Dramatic Tributes
items.summary: Performances included gospel hymns and a series of dramatic letters to Dr. King written from the perspectives of Marian Wright Edelman, Maya Angelou, and Diane Nash Bevel.

items.title: Drum Major Awards
items.summary: The center awarded its 2024 Drum Major Awards for community advocacy and cultural legacy to Joseph M. Jones, Frances N. Nwajei, Richard Caraviello, and posthumously to Dorothy Elizabeth Tucker.

items.title: Liturgical Dance and Poetry
items.summary: Pastor Teresa J. Cotter presented a ministry in dance, followed by a musical and poetic performance by Medford Poet Laureate Vijaya Sundaram.

items.title: Keynote Address: Policing and Reform
items.summary: Retired Boston Police Special Officer Darryl W. Owens delivered a keynote on the necessity of de-escalation, implicit bias training, and transparency in law enforcement to build community trust.

items.title: Charge to the Community and Closing
items.summary: Reverend Wendy Miller Olapade delivered a charge to practice nonviolence and sign the 'Be Love' pledge before concluding with announcements regarding upcoming Duggar Park renovations.
